study.title: The LORD reigns in fire and light
study.intro: Psalm 97 announces that the LORD reigns and paints His coming in storm, fire and lightning. Mountains melt before Him, idol worshipers are shamed, and Zion rejoices at His judgments. The psalm ends by calling those who love the LORD to hate evil, trust His protection, and rejoice in the light He sows for the righteous.
study.context: Psalm 97 belongs to the 'LORD reigns' psalms of Book IV (Psalms 93-99). Verses 1-6 describe God's appearing with imagery drawn from Mount Sinai: cloud, darkness, fire and quaking earth. Verses 7-9 contrast the true God with worthless idols. Verses 10-12 turn to the people who love Him, promising protection, light and gladness. Hebrews 1:6 echoes verse 7 when it speaks of the angels worshiping the Son.
study.peopleNote: Moses is linked because the cloud, darkness, fire and trembling mountain recall God's appearing at Sinai when Moses led Israel. Jesus is linked because Hebrews 1:6 applies the call to worship in verse 7 to God's Son. God is never portrayed as a human body in planned art.

verses.title: The LORD reigns
verses.heading: Distant shores be glad
verses.meaning: The psalm begins with a royal announcement: 'The LORD reigns, let the earth rejoice; let the distant shores be glad.' God's rule is not a threat to be dreaded by the world but good news to be celebrated. The 'distant shores' were the far coastlands and islands at the edge of Israel's map. Even the most remote peoples are invited to gladness, because the true King is just and good.
verses.context: Psalm 93:1 and 96:10 make the same announcement: 'The LORD reigns.' Isaiah 42:10-12 calls the islands and coastlands to sing a new song. Revelation 19:6 echoes it with a great multitude crying, 'Hallelujah! For the Lord our God the Almighty reigns.'
explore: Distant shores
The coastlands and islands far from Israel, picturing the ends of the known world.
Reigns
Rules as King now, actively governing all things with authority and justice.
verses.reflect: How does knowing that God reigns change the way you read today's news?
verses.alt: Waves wash onto a quiet distant shoreline at sunrise with small boats.

verses.title: Clouds and darkness
verses.heading: A throne founded on justice
verses.meaning: Verse 2 holds mystery and certainty together: 'Clouds and darkness surround Him; righteousness and justice are His throne's foundation.' We cannot see all of God; He is hidden in cloud and beyond our understanding. Yet what we cannot see does not leave us guessing about His character. The very base of His rule is righteousness and justice, so even His hiddenness can be trusted.
verses.context: Exodus 19:9 says God came to Moses 'in a dense cloud.' Deuteronomy 4:11 recalls the mountain blazing with fire amid darkness and thick cloud. Psalm 89:14 also says righteousness and justice are the foundation of God's throne.
explore: Clouds and darkness
Images of God's hidden majesty, recalling His appearing at Mount Sinai.
Foundation
The base that holds up a throne; God's rule rests on what is right and just.
verses.reflect: When God's ways feel cloudy to you, what do you know for sure about His character?
verses.alt: Heavy storm clouds gather over a dark mountain with a bright edge of light.

verses.title: Fire goes before Him
verses.heading: Foes consumed
verses.meaning: Verse 3 says, 'Fire goes before Him and consumes His foes on every side.' Fire in Scripture often shows God's holy presence: it purifies, it lights the way, and it destroys what opposes Him. Those who set themselves against God cannot stand before such holiness. For His people this is comfort, since no enemy can outlast the Lord who goes before them.
verses.context: Hebrews 12:29 says, 'Our God is a consuming fire.' Exodus 13:21 describes a pillar of fire leading Israel by night. Daniel 7:10 pictures a river of fire flowing from before the Ancient of Days.
explore: Consuming fire
God's holiness pictured as fire that removes everything evil and opposed to Him.
On every side
Complete surrounding, so no foe escapes by hiding in any direction.
verses.reflect: Is there anything in your life that God's holy fire needs to burn away?
verses.alt: A wall of flame moves across a dry plain beneath a stormy sky.

verses.title: Lightning lights the world
verses.heading: The earth trembles
verses.meaning: Verse 4 continues the storm picture: 'His lightning illuminates the world; the earth sees and trembles.' A lightning flash suddenly shows everything hidden in the dark. In the same way, God's appearing exposes all things. The earth's trembling is the right response of creation to its Creator's power, a reminder that God is not small, tame or easily managed.
verses.context: Exodus 19:16 records thunder, lightning and a thick cloud on Sinai, so the people trembled. Psalm 77:18 says, 'Your lightning lit up the world; the earth trembled and quaked.' Revelation 4:5 describes flashes of lightning coming from God's throne.
explore: Illuminates
Lights up brightly, revealing what was hidden in darkness.
Trembles
Shakes with awe and fear before God's overwhelming power and presence.
verses.reflect: What does it look like for you to approach God with both trust and holy awe?
verses.alt: Bright lightning splits a night sky over a wide valley and village.

verses.title: Mountains melt like wax
verses.heading: Lord of all the earth
verses.meaning: Verse 5 says, 'The mountains melt like wax at the presence of the LORD, before the Lord of all the earth.' Mountains are the most solid, permanent things people know. Yet before God they soften like candle wax near a flame. Nothing in creation is strong enough to resist His presence. He is not a local god of one hill but the Lord of all the earth.
verses.context: Micah 1:4 says the mountains melt beneath the LORD like wax before fire. Nahum 1:5 says the mountains quake before Him and the hills melt away. Joshua 3:11 calls the LORD 'the Lord of all the earth' as Israel crossed the Jordan.
explore: Like wax
Soft wax melts quickly near heat, showing how creation yields before God.
Lord of all the earth
A title declaring God's rule over every land, not only Israel.
verses.reflect: What 'mountain' in your life seems immovable but is small before God?
verses.alt: Rocky mountain slopes glow in hazy heat as mist pours down them.

verses.title: The heavens proclaim
verses.heading: All peoples see His glory
verses.meaning: Verse 6 says, 'The heavens proclaim His righteousness; all the peoples see His glory.' The sky itself becomes a preacher. The heavens declare not only God's power but His righteousness, His rightness in all He does. His glory is not kept secret for a few; all peoples are able to see it. God wants to be known by the whole world.
verses.context: Psalm 19:1 says, 'The heavens declare the glory of God.' Psalm 50:6 says, 'The heavens proclaim His righteousness, for God Himself is Judge.' Isaiah 40:5 promises that the glory of the LORD will be revealed and all people will see it.
explore: Proclaim
To announce publicly, as a herald announces a king's decree.
Glory
The weighty, shining greatness of God made visible in His works and presence.
verses.reflect: Where did you notice God's glory in creation recently?
verses.alt: A vast starry sky arches over many tents of different peoples.

verses.title: Idols put to shame
verses.heading: Worship Him, all you gods
verses.meaning: Verse 7 says, 'All worshipers of images are put to shame—those who boast in idols. Worship Him, all you gods!' When the true God appears, every substitute is exposed as empty. People who trusted idols are embarrassed to see their gods helpless. Even whatever powers people call 'gods' are commanded to bow before the LORD. Nothing else deserves the honor that belongs to Him alone.
verses.context: Isaiah 44:9 says those who make idols are nothing and will be put to shame. Hebrews 1:6 applies this call to worship to the Son: 'Let all God's angels worship Him.' 1 John 5:21 warns, 'Little children, keep yourselves from idols.'
explore: Images
Carved or cast figures that people worshiped in place of the living God.
Boast in idols
To take pride and confidence in false gods that cannot see, hear or save.
verses.reflect: What modern 'idol' tempts you to boast in something other than God?
verses.alt: A toppled stone statue lies cracked in the dust beside an empty shrine.

verses.title: Zion rejoices
verses.heading: Towns of Judah exult
verses.meaning: Verse 8 shifts to God's people: 'Zion hears and rejoices, and the towns of Judah exult because of Your judgments, O LORD.' What makes idol worshipers ashamed makes God's people glad. His judgments mean wrongs are set right and evil is not allowed the last word. Jerusalem and the small towns around it celebrate together, because God's justice is good news for those who trust Him.
verses.context: Psalm 48:11 says, 'Mount Zion is glad, the daughters of Judah rejoice on account of Your judgments.' Revelation 19:1-2 praises God because His judgments are true and just. Isaiah 26:9 says when God's judgments come, the world learns righteousness.
explore: Zion
The hill of Jerusalem where God's temple stood, standing for God's people.
Judgments
God's decisions and acts that set things right and deal with evil.
verses.reflect: Why can God's justice be a source of joy rather than only fear for His people?
verses.alt: Villagers in small hill towns dance in the streets with tambourines.

verses.title: Most High over all
verses.heading: Exalted above all gods
verses.meaning: Verse 9 explains the joy: 'For You, O LORD, are Most High over all the earth; You are exalted far above all gods.' The psalm speaks directly to God now. 'Most High' is a title of supreme rank: no ruler, power or rival stands above Him. He is not slightly greater than other gods; He is exalted 'far above' them, in a category all His own.
verses.context: Psalm 83:18 says, 'You alone, whose name is the LORD, are Most High over all the earth.' Psalm 95:3 calls the LORD 'a great King above all gods.' Ephesians 1:21 says Christ is seated far above every ruler, authority, power and name.
explore: Most High
A title for God meaning the highest ruler over all heaven and earth.
Exalted
Lifted up and honored above all others in rank, power and worth.
verses.reflect: How would your fears change if you truly believed God is far above them all?
verses.alt: A high mountain peak rises far above lower hills under clear sky.

verses.title: Hate evil
verses.heading: He preserves His saints
verses.meaning: Verse 10 gives a command and a promise: 'Hate evil, O you who love the LORD! He preserves the souls of His saints; He delivers them from the hand of the wicked.' Love for God naturally produces a hatred of evil, because evil harms what God loves. And those who love Him are not left alone; He guards their lives and rescues them from those who would destroy them.
verses.context: Amos 5:15 says, 'Hate evil and love good.' Romans 12:9 urges, 'Abhor what is evil; cling to what is good.' Proverbs 2:8 says God guards the course of the just and protects the way of His saints.
explore: Saints
God's faithful, devoted people, set apart to belong to Him.
Preserves
Guards and keeps safe, watching over a life so it is not lost.
verses.reflect: Is there an evil you have grown comfortable with that love for God calls you to hate?
verses.alt: A shepherd guides a small flock away from a dark ravine to safety.

verses.title: Light shines
verses.heading: Gladness for the upright
verses.meaning: Verse 11 says, 'Light shines on the righteous, gladness on the upright in heart.' The image may also be of light being sown like seed, spreading across a field. God scatters light and joy over those who walk with Him. Even when they pass through darkness, light is planted ahead of them and will spring up. Gladness is God's gift, not something forced.
verses.context: Proverbs 4:18 says the path of the righteous is like the first gleam of dawn, shining brighter until midday. Psalm 112:4 says light dawns in the darkness for the upright. John 8:12 records Jesus saying, 'I am the light of the world.'
explore: Light
Image of God's favor, guidance, truth and life shining on His people.
Upright in heart
People whose inner lives are honest and straight before God.
verses.reflect: Where do you need God's light to break into a dark place in your life?
verses.alt: Morning sunlight spreads across a freshly sown field and a farmer.

verses.title: Rejoice in the LORD
verses.heading: Praise His holy name
verses.meaning: The psalm closes, 'Rejoice in the LORD, you righteous ones, and praise His holy name.' After storm, fire and judgment, the final word is joy. The righteous do not rejoice mainly in their circumstances but 'in the LORD' Himself. Praise of His holy name means honoring all He has revealed of Himself: His holiness, justice, power and faithful love.
verses.context: Philippians 4:4 says, 'Rejoice in the Lord always. I will say it again: Rejoice!' Psalm 33:1 calls the righteous to sing joyfully to the LORD. Psalm 30:4 says, 'Sing to the LORD, O you His saints, and praise His holy name.'
explore: Rejoice in
To find joy with God as its source and center, not just in good events.
Holy name
God's revealed character and reputation, set apart from everything common.
verses.reflect: What about God's character can you rejoice in today, regardless of your circumstances?
verses.alt: A family sings together outside their home as evening light glows.
